messages:
Maria - AE: quick ask — prospect (healthcare infra) wants a 4-week POC. Need scoping help: success criteria, eval/prompt sets, timeline, and integration plan (SDK auth, streaming, rate limits, retries). also they asked about Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and SSO/VPC. @Raj @Lin can you help?

Raj - SolutionsEng: happy to. first pass checklist: 1) pick 2–3 primary use cases (e.g., clinical note summarization, patient Q&A, triage classification). 2) define success metrics per use case (latency p95, response accuracy / exact-match or ROUGE/F1, hallucination rate threshold). 3) prompt/eval plan (seed set + holdout). 4) infra constraints (throughput, concurrency). 5) security gating (VPC, KMS).

Raj - SolutionsEng: suggested success criteria (example):
- Summarization: avg compression 6x, ROUGE-L >= 0.55 on holdout (100 prompts)
- Q&A: exact-match >= 0.7 on curated 150 question set; hallucination < 5%
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for short prompts, p95 < 800ms for long sequences
- Cost: target <= $0.10 per 1k output tokens for Hosted POC (adjust for Dedicated)

Raj - SolutionsEng: prompts/evals: pick ~200 seed prompts across edge cases, hold out 20% for blind eval. include adversarial prompts that cause hallucinations. run automated evals nightly during week 3.

Lin - SE: integration notes: use Redwood SDK (node/python) for fastest path. auth is bearer token: set via env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. streaming works over chunked responses — default reconnect/backoff on 429 or network error. rate limits: Hosted default quota is modest for new keys; for POC we can request a temporary bump to meet concurrency.

Lin - SE: quick examples:
Node (streaming):
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1', messages });
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta); }
```

cURL (simple):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"summarize: ..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Lin - SE: retries: exponential backoff, jitter. For streaming, resume by re-sending last token index if connection drops; for most POCs simpler to fall back to non-streaming retry with idempotency key.

Maria - AE: thanks. on pricing — can you give a rough Hosted vs Dedicated POC cost range? they want a budget number for procurement.

Lin - SE: rough rules of thumb (very approximate): Hosted small POC (low throughput, <100k tokens/day) => $1k–$3k/month. Dedicated short POC (reserved capacity, 1–2 GPUs for 4 weeks) => $6k–$18k for the POC depending on GPU type and support. We can also offer a short-term discounted trial or credits — check with finance/sales ops for approval.

Claire - Security: security checklist items we'll need to sign off: SSO (SAML/OIDC), SOC 2 attestation, DPA, subprocessor list. For Private/VPC: we support VPC peering or private endpoint + KMS integration for key control. If they need on-prem, that's a separate engineering effort — flag early. Also ask them to provide an initial security questionnaire (NDA first if they want details).

Ben - CSM: POC playbook suggestion: Week 0: kickoff + SSO/keys + allowlist. Week 1: infra + model selection + baseline eval. Week 2: integration of SDK + streaming + sample prompts. Week 3: run batch evals + tune prompts, run monitoring hooks. Week 4: finalize reports, handoff to engineering and ops. Success = pass holdout > thresholds + reliable infra at target throughput.

Maria - AE: customer asked about rate limits and quotas (RPS, tokens/sec). Can we commit to numbers for their procurement doc?

Lin - SE: we can commit to target throughput for Dedicated (SLA) and best-effort for Hosted. For procurement doc use: Hosted default soft limit: 60 req/s per key, token throughput depends on model (roughly 200–500 tokens/s per concurrent stream for medium GPUs). For Dedicated we can specify exact p95 latency and throughput after we size pool. We'll include a surge/burst policy.

Raj - SolutionsEng: next actions I propose: 1) Maria to share exact POC use cases & expected TPS. 2) I'll draft a 1-page POC scope + success criteria doc and sample prompt set (100–200). 3) Claire to send security checklist template. 4) Lin to list integration code snippets and default rate limits. 5) Ben to own onboarding schedule.

Maria - AE: perfect. I'll ping the prospect to collect use case details and expected concurrency. Aim to have a draft scope by EOD tomorrow. cc @Claire @Lin @Raj @Ben :thumbsup:

Ben - CSM: noted. I'll prepare a monitoring and eval dashboard template to track metrics during the POC and share by tomorrow morning.

Claire - Security: I'll attach the standard security questionnaire and DPA to the thread once we have the prospect's legal contact. LMK if they require SOC2/ISO artifacts now.

Maria - AE: thanks all — this is super helpful. I'll update thread with the customer's use-case doc and procurement timeline later today. 🙂
